_incomplete_by_construction: An object nobody ever wrote down is absent from this list and therefore invisible to the check, exactly as it is invisible to every other instrument here. That is the honest limit and it is not a reason to skip the list: thirty rounds of per-pixel comparison never surfaced a missing doorway, and this file would have carried it from round one. The list GROWS when the target is read again; it is not a closed set.
_law: Every entry resolves to BUILT (a mass) or to a declared gap WITH A REASON. `absent_baseline` may shrink and may never grow.

_signoff_provenance: OWNER ORDER 2026-08-08, given as `ลุยหมด` in reply to an itemised recommendation that carried, per id, the measurement behind it and my recommendation. The TEXT below was written by the builder under that instruction — it is not the owner's own prose, and a reader should weigh it as `the owner approved this reasoning after reading it`, not as `the owner wrote this`. Recording the difference matters because this field exists precisely so the builder cannot widen its own exemption list: if the distinction is not written down, a builder-authored signoff and an owner-authored one become indistinguishable, which is the same failure the field was built to prevent one level up.

absent_baseline_signoff.nightstand_books: DECLARED GAP r35 — NOT MEASURABLE FROM THIS REFERENCE, and that is a measurement, not a shrug. The stack is ~25 px tall and crossed by the bird's legs and by printed text. Three independent sub-pixel fits were run and all three failed: top edge rms 5.90 px, bottom edge rms 5.95 px, left end sigma 7.94 px — against the 0.17-0.85 px this same image yields on real arrises (the shade flank 0.170, the headboard end 0.56, the plinth 0.159). Back-projected, the height comes out 28 +- 26 mm, a bound running from 2 mm (no books) to 54 mm (two thick ones), so it separates nothing. R10: the moment a pass says a dimension is unmeasurable, typing a number for it is the defect. Reopen with a higher-resolution reference or a second view.
absent_baseline_signoff.nightstand_bird: DECLARED GAP r35 — ACQUIRE per R8 (an animal figure is free-form; hand modelling is forbidden), and acquisition CANNOT LAND, for a blocker that is structural rather than about this object: `trn002_build.py` has NO import path at all (0 matches for gltf/glb/import_scene/libraries.load), so no fetched mesh can enter this lane's scene whatever its source or licence. That is why 26 assets already sit cached in assets/shared/ unused. SECOND, INDEPENDENT reason to leave it out even once the importer exists: the reference's bird is unmistakably an Eames House Bird (Vitra), and R8 is explicit that TRADE DRESS IS NOT CLEARED BY A LICENCE — a CC0 replica of a protected product design is still trade dress in a commercial render. Building the glTF import path is the unblocking task, and it is a lane of its own, not a step in a styling round.

_ratchet_precondition: SEEDED 2026-08-08 by owner order. This file was untracked, so `rule_gate.baseline_ratchet` failed closed and blocked every render in the lane — intended, not a bug: a ratchet with no committed history is a list. It was committed in TWO steps on purpose. Commit 1 seeds THIS state (four ids in `absent_baseline`, `closet_oak_depth` already dropped because r34 built it). Commit 2 adds the widening below. Doing both in one commit would have put the five new exemptions inside the seed, where the ratchet has nothing to compare them against — the widening would never have been checked, which is the only thing the ratchet exists to do.
